title: K-flat scalar cone and its natural total-tensor model
statement:
Let $\mathcal A$ be a closed braided monoidal Grothendieck abelian category with additive tensor and functorial flat resolutions [def-sp-grothendieck-abelian, def-sfb-monoidal-category, lem-sfb-derived-monoidal]. Let $B$ be a commutative ring acting linearly on $\mathcal A$, with $(b u)\otimes v=b(u\otimes v)=u\otimes(b v)$ for morphisms $u,v$ and $b\in B$. Fix $b\in B$, and put
$$P_b=\operatorname{Cone}(b:\mathbf1[0]\to\mathbf1[0]),$$
with the cochain and cone conventions of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Then $P_b$ is K-flat for the total tensor product and two-sided quasi-isomorphism convention of [def-sfb-preserves-kflat-quasi-iso]. For every unbounded cochain complex $C$ there is an isomorphism of complexes
$$\operatorname{Tot}(C\otimes P_b)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Cone}(b:C\to C),$$
natural in chain maps $C\to C'$. If $Q$ is cochain localization, its composite with the canonical K-flat tensor comparison gives isomorphisms
$$QC\otimes^{\mathbf L}QP_b\xrightarrow{\sim}Q\operatorname{Cone}(b:C\to C),$$
natural in $C$. Thus the displayed cochain cone functor inverts quasi-isomorphisms after localization and descends with these isomorphisms to a functor naturally isomorphic to $-\otimes^{\mathbf L}QP_b$ on $D(\mathcal A)$.

proof.text: Use the existing upstream tensorScalarConeIso' and its hom naturality to assemble Φ by NatIso.ofComponents. Similarly assemble θ from tensorScalarConeIso and tensorScalarConeIso_hom_naturality. The latter is, by definition, asIso(μ Q C P_b) followed by Q.mapIso(Φ_C), so the required equality for θ.hom.app is reflexive. Invertibility of μ is the upstream isIso_μ_scalarCone instance, obtained from kFlat_scalarCone and the derived monoidal computation. These are the existing scalar-cone and derived-tensor constructions, not new choices of cone data.

proof.text: For a quasi-isomorphism f:C→D, Q(f) is invertible. Naturality of μ gives Q(f ▷ P_b) = μ(C,P_b)⁻¹ ≫ (Q(f) ▷ Q(P_b)) ≫ μ(D,P_b). All three factors are invertible by step 1 and functoriality. DerivedCategory.isIso_Q_map_iff_quasiIso therefore shows that f ▷ P_b is a quasi-isomorphism. Braiding naturality gives P_b ◁ f = β(P_b,C).hom ≫ (f ▷ P_b) ≫ β(P_b,D).inv. Quasi-isomorphisms contain isomorphisms and are closed under composition, so P_b ◁ f is also a quasi-isomorphism. The two whiskerings are definitionally the two HomologicalComplex.tensorHom maps in IsKFlatForTotalTensor, giving exactly its two conjuncts.

proof.text: For a quasi-isomorphism f:C→D, naturality of θ from step 1 gives (F_b ⋙ Q).map f = θ_C⁻¹ ≫ (Q(f) ▷ Q(P_b)) ≫ θ_D. Each factor is invertible, so F_b ⋙ Q inverts quasi-isomorphisms. This uses only the already constructed θ and that Q inverts quasi-isomorphisms; no long exact sequence or five lemma is needed.

proof.text: Choose the descended functor explicitly as F = tensorRight(Q(P_b)), with η = θ and δ = Iso.refl F. The required compatibility reduces to the identity law 𝟙 ≫ θ_C = θ_C. Thus the existing derived right tensor functor already supplies the required descent; choosing a separate localization lift and then comparing it is unnecessary.
